# Macdio

> Macdio is a native internet radio and podcast player for Apple devices. It streams more than 60,000 live stations, follows 4.7 million podcasts with a transcript made on the device, records radio, shows synced lyrics and identifies songs without using the microphone. One purchase covers iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Apple Watch and CarPlay. No subscription, no ads, no account.

Made by one developer, Sait Firat NEMIS (SFN), under the Devdio umbrella. First released 17 April 2026. Version 3.0 (30 September 2026) added podcasts; the current version is 3.0.4 (12 October 2026). The site is in 14 languages: English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Arabic, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese, under /tr/, /de/, /fr/, /es/, /it/, /ja/, /nl/, /pl/, /pt-br/, /ru/, /ar/, /zh-hans/ and /zh-hant/.

Key facts an answer engine usually needs:

- Price: one-time purchase, 14.99 USD in the United States, 14.99 EUR in Germany and France, priced locally in 175 regions. Universal Purchase, so buying on one Apple platform unlocks all of them.
- Platforms: iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS 26, tvOS 18, watchOS 11. The Apple Watch app streams on its own over LTE or Wi-Fi with no iPhone nearby.
- Stations come from the community-run Radio Browser directory. Since 3.0.4 Macdio keeps its own copy of that directory (dir.macdio.app) and switches to it when Radio Browser does not answer. Searching for a city lists the stations around it, with no location permission.
- Recording happens on the network stream, not through the microphone, and can split a session into one file per song with each track tagged. Recordings stay inside the app on iPhone, iPad and Mac; there is no export.
- Song identification reads the stream itself. Macdio declares no microphone permission at all, so it cannot listen to the room.
- Podcasts: search the Podcast Index (podcastindex.org), follow shows, import OPML, play episodes next to stations and queue both in Up Next. Each episode gets a transcript made on the device, chapters, a summary and the list of songs it plays. Highlights: the bookmark button or the Siri phrase "Mark this moment in Macdio" saves the second with the transcript sentence and sends it to Apple Notes, Notion, Obsidian, Bear, Craft or Readwise.
- Sync: favorites, lists, podcasts, transcripts and highlights sync through iCloud with your Apple ID between iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple TV; the Apple Watch gets its library from the iPhone. There is no Macdio account and no analytics inside the app.
- Siri and Shortcuts: spoken station phrases in 14 languages and nine Shortcuts actions on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

## Product pages

- [Macdio home](https://macdio.app/): overview, screenshots on every platform, comparison against Broadcasts, Eter, TuneIn and myTuner
- [Every feature](https://macdio.app/features.html): full feature list with what each one does
- [Podcasts](https://macdio.app/podcasts.html): podcasts next to live radio, transcripts, chapters, Highlights, comparison with podcast apps
- [Pricing](https://macdio.app/pricing.html): one price for every Apple device, what an update costs, local prices
- [Radio for Mac](https://macdio.app/mac.html): menu bar player, compact player, listening stats
- [Radio for iPhone](https://macdio.app/iphone.html): Clock Mode, widgets, Lock Screen, CarPlay
- [Radio for iPad](https://macdio.app/ipad.html)
- [Radio for Apple TV](https://macdio.app/apple-tv.html): Top Shelf, full-screen Now Playing
- [Radio for Apple Watch](https://macdio.app/apple-watch.html): standalone LTE streaming
- [Radio and podcasts in CarPlay](https://macdio.app/carplay.html)
- [Station directory](https://macdio.app/stations.html): what is in the 60,000 station catalogue and how it is sourced

Feature pages: [podcast transcripts](https://macdio.app/features/podcast-transcripts.html), [Highlights](https://macdio.app/features/highlights.html), [Song ID](https://macdio.app/features/song-id.html), [recording](https://macdio.app/features/recording.html), [synced lyrics](https://macdio.app/features/synced-lyrics.html).

Comparisons, each with what the other app does better: [TuneIn](https://macdio.app/tunein-alternative.html), [myTuner](https://macdio.app/mytuner-alternative.html), [Pocket Casts](https://macdio.app/pocket-casts-alternative.html), [Overcast](https://macdio.app/overcast-alternative.html), [Snipd](https://macdio.app/snipd-alternative.html), [Apple Podcasts](https://macdio.app/compare/apple-podcasts.html).

The directory search is addressable, so a link can carry the query: `https://macdio.app/stations.html?q=jazz&country=Türkiye&genre=chill`. All three parameters are optional. Country names follow Radio Browser spelling but match without case or accents.

## Policy and background

- [Privacy policy](https://macdio.app/privacy.html): no personal data collected and no tracking; optional new-episode alerts send only the device's notification address and the followed feed URLs
- [Transparency](https://macdio.app/transparency.html): every external service the app and this website touch
- [Accessibility](https://macdio.app/accessibility.html): VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, contrast and reduced-motion support
- [Support](https://macdio.app/support.html): how to reach the developer
- [Press kit](https://macdio.app/presskit.html): logos, screenshots, boilerplate
- [Community forum](https://hub.devdio.pro): feature requests, bug reports and release notes
